# Tetsubi

> Tetsubi is a music player app for iPhone and Mac that plays your own music library from a Jellyfin server. It is a Jellyfin music client: it streams from your server and downloads albums for offline listening. No Tetsubi account, no subscription, no adverts and no tracking. Made by DEKIRU Ltd. Coming soon to the App Store.

Tetsubi was made with Claude, Anthropic's AI, under its developer's direction and review.

Tetsubi works only with Jellyfin servers (not Plex, Emby, Navidrome or Subsonic). It brings an album-first, Plexamp-like experience to Jellyfin; it is not made by or connected with Plex or the Jellyfin project. An Android version is in the works and coming soon.

## Features

- Sign in with Jellyfin Quick Connect (a six-digit code) or username and password; login kept in the Keychain
- Home: On This Day (albums released on today's date in past years), Favourites, Recently Played, Recently Added, Random
- Library: albums, artists and favourites; grid or list; sort, filter and A–Z index
- Search, including offline search of downloads
- Album downloads for offline listening: original quality, or FLAC, ALAC, AAC, MP3, Opus or WAV; background downloads with pause, resume and retry
- Gapless playback, shuffle and repeat
- Blurred album-art backgrounds; progress bar coloured from the album art
- 10-band equaliser with presets, and a spectrum visualiser
- AirPlay; lock-screen, Control Centre and Dynamic Island controls, with artwork even offline
- Siri ("Play <album> in Tetsubi") and Shortcuts
- Maniac Mode: albums play start to finish with no skipping, shuffle or scrubbing
- "About the artist" from MusicBrainz, Wikidata and Wikipedia
- Lower-quality streaming on mobile data (user-chosen), volume normalisation
- Mac app
- CarPlay

## Requirements

- A Jellyfin server with a music library, and an account on it
- iPhone or Mac (Android coming soon)
- To listen away from home: a VPN to the home network or a secure https address for the server

## Privacy

Tetsubi collects no personal data. It connects only to the user's own Jellyfin server, plus MusicBrainz, Wikidata and Wikipedia for artist information (sending only the artist's name or MusicBrainz ID).
